bibliographic_review_management.tier_rationale: Supporting for nanosatellite MBSE and preliminary design/toolchain integration; not a core EPS-specific MBSE verification study.

bibliographic_review_management.venue: IEEE Systems Conference (SysCon) inferred from DOI/provenance

source_database_query_route.query: "MBSE Challenges in the Concurrent Preliminary Design of CubeSats: Nanospace Study"
("CubeSat" OR cubesat OR nanosatellite) AND ("model-based systems engineering" OR MBSE OR SysML) AND (mission OR architecture OR design)

RQ1.rationale: Directly addresses generic CubeSat preliminary-design modeling with known unknowns, SysML artifacts, dependency graphs, DSMs, and reusable scripts/workflow. EPS/power is included as a budget but not a full EPS model.

RQ2.rationale: Claims traceability, reuse, communication, consistency, cost/time, automation, and decision support from MBSE/Nanospace, but evidence is mostly conceptual or from one case and not EPS-specific.

RQ3.rationale: Includes pre-physical requirement/constraint checking for power and system design, but no formal EPS verification procedure model, verification matrix, or test-procedure integration.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: Part of the Nanospace open-source CubeSat concurrent-design toolchain lineage (Gateau et al. 2021) and related DSM/MB2DM work. The CREME use case builds on ISAE-SUPAERO/ONERA CubeSat experience and references EyeSat/EntrySat heritage.

study_context_population.mission_platform: CREME CubeSat Radiation Environment Monitoring Experiment, a nanosatellite/CubeSat mission for LEO radiation-environment measurement; example iterations consider 2U feasibility and then 3U sizing.
study_context_population.size_form_factor: CubeSat; paper defines 1U as 10 cm x 10 cm x 10 cm up to 2 kg; CREME payload is 1.5U, initial spacecraft at least 2U, later 3U scenario.
study_context_population.mission_domain: Space-weather/radiation environment monitoring in Low Earth Orbit; charged-particle detector payload.
study_context_population.organization_type: Academic/university-led platform at ISAE-SUPAERO with ONERA payload and CSUT exploitation perspective; open-source/educational tool context.
study_context_population.project_maturity: Approved by Occitanie region and started late 2020; paper uses a simplified subset of requirements/constraints during preliminary design.
study_context_population.eps_relevance_notes: Power subsystem is treated through solar-panel generation, battery capacity/DoD, payload/platform loads, eclipse duration, and power-budget plots; not a complete EPS architecture/verification model.
context_quotes: 'Nanospace is a web application dedicated to facilitate concurrent engineering during the preliminary design phase of CubeSats.'
'The CubeSat Radiation Environment Monitoring Experiment (CREME) project ... objective is to measure the radiation environment in Low Earth Orbit (LEO).'
'Telecommunication and power are traditionally the most critical subsystems to ensure mission survival.'

stated_objective_pain_point: Integrate MBSE with the open-source Nanospace concurrent-design environment for CubeSat preliminary design.
Improve communication and system-level coordination among experts; reduce manual systems-engineer monitoring of process order, consistency, and up-to-date shared data.
Capture CubeSat parameter dependencies so DSMs/dependency graphs can guide iterations and change propagation.
Archive/reuse CubeSat design knowledge from prior missions and support faster architecture inspection.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.system_boundary_and_abstraction: Simplified preliminary-design CubeSat model covering mission/orbit, telecommunications, on-board computing/data storage, energy and power, structure, payload, and ground segment parameters. The paper uses subset requirements/constraints and preliminary estimates, assumes circular orbit and sun-pointing when not in eclipse, omits mission modes, and excludes ADCS, radiation, and thermal considerations from the example.
deliberately_minimal_or_excluded: Only subset of CREME requirements/constraints due to space constraints.
Mission modes not discussed; authors state concept can be extended to include them.
ADCS, radiation, and thermal considerations omitted from example but described as fundamental for real missions.
Initial power/platform values use rough expert estimates and worst-case scenario assumptions.
mbse_objective_scope_artifacts.required_prior_behavioral_domain_knowled: Method still relies on expert starting values and experience for known unknowns, flight-proven component preferences, margins, and trade-off decisions. MBSE is proposed to capture/reuse this knowledge through dependencies and models but does not eliminate expert judgment.
generality_reuse_mechanism: specific-mission model with reusable method only
key_quotes: 'MBSE can be used to capture the system dependencies represented in Figs.1 and 2, allowing to reuse knowledge from previous CubeSat missions.'
'From these system models, using a dedicated algorithm it is possible to generate Design Structure Matrices (DSMs) from a SysML model.'
'The models contain the functions related to the CubeSat, the space environment, the launch segment, the ground segment, the customer and the legislative and regulatory institutions.'

generality_reuse_mechanism_v1_1_reasonin.rationale: The paper supports reuse mainly as a transferable preliminary-design method around Nanospace, scripts, SysML-to-DSM transformation, and dependency/parameter abstractions. The CREME demonstration is still a specific use case, so mission-agnostic architecture should not be coded. v1.1 labels are supported because the model is high-level, parameter/interface/dependency-focused, and deliberately omits detailed behavior/modes/domains, while claiming the diagrams can be reshaped for new missions.

RQ1: Useful system-level CubeSat modeling approach for preliminary design can be built around requirements/constraints, discipline parameter dependencies, DSMs, and a Nanospace DB/API-backed workflow.
The method explicitly handles known unknowns through expert-provided initial values, margins, and iterative simulation rather than requiring a complete behavioral model upfront.
EPS is represented only as preliminary power-budget/electrical-architecture elements, not a general EPS MBSE reference model.
RQ2: Claims MBSE/Nanospace value in reuse, traceability, consistency, communication, automation, and decision support; strongest case evidence is scripted requirement checking and design trade guidance.
Reliability and mission assurance are indirect via constraint checking (DoD, link, reentry), not via reliability modeling or flight/test outcomes.
Reproducibility is supported by open-source/AGPL intent but limited by unavailable SysML model/details in markdown.
RQ3: Pre-physical design checks exist for power and requirements via simulations and Nanospace status flags, but no formal EPS verification-procedure model, verification matrix, test procedure, SIL/HIL, or automated test chain is presented.
